_note: The team block: what a side does without instructions (VISION §3, the role as a default intention, 2026-11-12). Each outfield player keeps his role's place inside a block: depth from the defensive line (0) to the forward line (1), and width from left (0) to right (1), read from the formation. The block follows the ball: the defensive line sits behind the ball (further behind and higher up the pitch when the side has the ball), within a minimum and a maximum distance from its own goal; the block shifts towards the ball's side. With the ball the side stretches (longer, wider), without it it compacts (shorter, narrower). The coach's instructions (L2) will move these numbers; they never script the players.
_source: Order of magnitude of a real team's shape: a compact block out of possession is about 30-35 m deep and 35-45 m wide; in possession it stretches to about 45 m and uses most of the width. The other values are arbitrary, declared, to be calibrated at L3.
